obligation: G033 -- the draft-tier re-aim, and whether a packer would settle it
question: G057 priced the plane draft tier from ps/element and found it 1.55x from break-even. Building a packer would test whether that per-kernel number transfers to a real artifact's token time. This calibrates the prediction against three artifacts that ALREADY exist, so the margin can be compared to the actual prediction error.
verdict: The ps/element model predicts real artifact token time to within 5.83% across three artifacts spanning two body codecs. The draft tier is 1.55x from break-even, a margin 9x larger than the model's worst observed error. A packer would confirm a number, not discover one, and G057's refutation stands without it.
what_a_packer_WOULD_still_test: whether a plane BODY is coherent at all -- G033 measured the ladder dominated by flat codes in function space, so a plane artifact is expected to fail the capability gate, and that is a separate question from the speed one settled here.
honest_caveat: This is a decision NOT to run an experiment, justified by a measured margin. It is the same class of reasoning that was wrong twice this session (G035, G053), where a family was dismissed on its weaker member. The difference is that this dismissal rests on a quantified margin against a measured error bar rather than on the absence of a test.
